title: Weak-equivalence invariance of strict pullbacks along Kan fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $X_0\xrightarrow{f}X\xleftarrow{g}X_1$ and $Y_0\xrightarrow{f\prime}Y\xleftarrow{g\prime}Y_1$ be cospans of small simplicial sets, and let $\alpha:X_0\to Y_0$, $\beta:X\to Y$, and $\gamma:X_1\to Y_1$ all be weak homotopy equivalences satisfying $\beta f=f\prime\alpha$ and $\beta g=g\prime\gamma$. Suppose $f$ and $f\prime$ are Kan fibrations. Then the induced map on strict pullbacks $X_0\times_X X_1\to Y_0\times_Y Y_1$, given degreewise by $(x_0,x_1)\mapsto(\alpha(x_0),\gamma(x_1))$, is a weak homotopy equivalence. No Kan-complex hypothesis on the six objects is imposed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109), weak-equivalence invariance of strict pullbacks along Kan fibrations; read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: First establish the fixed-base calculation, with no fibrancy assumptions on objects. Let $a:A\to Z$ and $b:B\to Z$ be Kan fibrations and let $r:A\to B$ be a weak homotopy equivalence with $br=a$. Set $D=A\times_Z B$. Both $D\to A$ and $D\to B$ are Kan fibrations: a horn lifting square for a projection is precisely a horn lifting square for the other original leg, with the prescribed coordinate retained. Factor the graph $(1_A,r):A\to D$ as a trivial cofibration $j:A\to M$ followed by a Kan fibration $k:M\to D$, using the model structure in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Write $s=\operatorname{pr}_A k$ and $t=\operatorname{pr}_B k$. Composition of Kan fibrations is a Kan fibration: lift the prescribed base simplex first through the second map and then through the first. Thus $s,t$ are Kan fibrations. The equalities $sj=1_A$ and $tj=r$, together with the model two-out-of-three axiom, make $s,t$ weak homotopy equivalences, hence trivial fibrations. Give $M$ the map $as=bt$ to $Z$; then all these maps, including $j$, are over $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109), statement read online 2026-10-17; agent proof by graph factorization and Kan--Quillen right properness, expanding the arbitrary-base comparison. Not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For any simplicial map $v:T\to Z$, pull the maps $s,t,j,r$ of step 1 back over $Z$ and denote them by $s_T,t_T,j_T,r_T$. The square with top $s_T:M\times_ZT\to A\times_ZT$, bottom $s:M\to A$, and vertical coordinate projections is a strict pullback: a pair $(m,(a,u))$ with $s(m)=a$ determines $(m,u)$, since $as(m)=v(u)$. The square with top $t_T:M\times_ZT\to B\times_ZT$ and bottom $t:M\to B$ is also a strict pullback: a pair $(m,(b,u))$ with $t(m)=b$ determines $(m,u)$, since $bt(m)=v(u)$. These identifications and their inverse coordinate projections commute with all simplicial operators. By the boundary-lifting characterization of trivial fibrations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], $s_T$ and $t_T$ are trivial fibrations. Indeed any boundary lifting problem projects to one for $s$ or $t$; pair its filler with the already prescribed $T$-simplex to obtain the required filler. This includes the boundary in dimension zero. The equations $s_Tj_T=1$ and $t_Tj_T=r_T$ hold degreewise. Since $s_T,t_T$ are weak homotopy equivalences, two-out-of-three first makes $j_T$ a weak homotopy equivalence and then makes $r_T$ one. This proves that a weak equivalence between two Kan fibrations over a fixed arbitrary base remains a weak equivalence after every base change.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109), statement read online 2026-10-17; agent proof by graph factorization and Kan--Quillen right properness, expanding the arbitrary-base comparison. Not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Return to the cospans of the statement. Put $E=Y_0\times_{Y,f\prime,\beta}X$, with projections $q:E\to Y_0$ and $p:E\to X$. The map $p$ is a Kan fibration by the horn lifting argument of step 1, applied to $f\prime$. Right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], applied to the weak equivalence $\beta:X\to Y$ and the Kan fibration $f\prime:Y_0\to Y$, makes $q$ a weak homotopy equivalence. The equality $f\prime\alpha=\beta f$ defines $h:X_0\to E$, $x_0\mapsto(\alpha(x_0),f(x_0))$. It satisfies $qh=\alpha$ and $ph=f$. Because $q$ and $\alpha$ are weak homotopy equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $h$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Its source and target structure maps $f:X_0\to X$ and $p:E\to X$ are both Kan fibrations, exactly as required for steps 1--2.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109), statement read online 2026-10-17; agent proof by graph factorization and Kan--Quillen right properness, expanding the arbitrary-base comparison. Not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply the fixed-base result of steps 1--2 to $h$ over $X$ and $g:X_1\to X$. It makes $h_g:X_0\times_X X_1\to E\times_X X_1$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Degreewise the target identifies with $Q=Y_0\times_{Y,f\prime,\beta g}X_1$ by $((y_0,x),x_1)\mapsto(y_0,x_1)$; its inverse inserts $x=g(x_1)$. Put $P'=Y_0\times_Y Y_1$. Its projection $P'\to Y_1$ is a Kan fibration by lifting a horn through $f\prime$ while retaining the prescribed $Y_1$ coordinate. Since $\beta g=g\prime\gamma$, the coordinate maps $(y_0,x_1)\mapsto((y_0,\gamma(x_1)),x_1)$ and $((y_0,y_1),x_1)\mapsto(y_0,x_1)$ are inverse simplicial isomorphisms $Q\cong P'\times_{Y_1}X_1$: the pullback equation $y_1=\gamma(x_1)$ and $f\prime(y_0)=g\prime(y_1)$ are equivalent to $f\prime(y_0)=\beta g(x_1)$. Under these formulas the map $Q\to P'$, $(y_0,x_1)\mapsto(y_0,\gamma(x_1))$, is exactly the pullback of the weak equivalence $\gamma:X_1\to Y_1$ along this Kan fibration. Right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] makes it a weak homotopy equivalence. Composing these two weak homotopy equivalences gives the desired map: on every simplex it is $(x_0,x_1)\mapsto(\alpha(x_0),\gamma(x_1))$. The coordinate formulas commute with faces and degeneracies, so this is the actual stated simplicial map, not merely a comparison up to homotopy. No step has assumed any of the six original objects Kan.
